description: Hi I am Debangana... I am interested in space and everything related to earth.
summary:
"The Baton of Silence" is an interactive, comic-style web story that teaches children about the equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars. Guided by Mira, a curious student, and Dr. Vance, a NASA scientist, kids explore five chapters. They fire a laser at the Apollo 11 mirror, poke lunar dirt with Surveyor 3, test Moon gravity and trigger a moonquake with the Apollo 15 buggy, blow dust off the Spirit rover's solar panels, and dig for ice with Phoenix. A final timeline connects every mission to its official NASA source.
It answers the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" by giving each silent machine a story and a purpose. Instead of reading dry facts, children interact with the machines and learn through Mira's questions, which feel like a real conversation. Each chapter shows how one machine passed the baton to the next generation of explorers.
This matters because children often assume old space hardware is just dead junk. Our project shows these machines still help us today: the Apollo 11 mirror still works, and Phoenix proved Mars hides water ice. It makes space history fun and accessible, and it inspires young learners to become future explorers.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

"The Baton of Silence" is an interactive web story that runs in any browser. Mira, a curious student, asks questions and Dr. Vance, a NASA scientist, answers them. Kids click through five chapters and interact with each machine: sending a laser pulse to the Apollo 11 mirror, poking the dirt with Surveyor 3, switching between Earth and Moon gravity and triggering a moonquake with the Apollo 15 buggy, blowing dust off Spirit, and digging for ice with Phoenix. A final timeline links every mission to its NASA source.

What benefits does it have?

With the help of this website

  • Children learn through play instead of reading dry facts.
  • It's free and needs no download, so it works on phones, tablets, and computers.
  • All facts are checked against NASA sources.

What is the intended impact?

It makes space history easy to understand for young learners.We want children to see that machines left on the Moon and Mars are not dead junk. They still teach us things today, such as the Apollo 11 mirror still working and Phoenix finding water ice. We hope this sparks curiosity and inspires kids to become future explorers.

What tools, languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Chatgpt,Codex,Gemini, Python, JavaScript,CSS, HTML, Canva

How is it creative?

Each abandoned machine becomes a character with its own story. The "baton" theme shows each machine handing its discoveries to the next generation of explorers. The conversation between Mira and Dr. Vance feels like a real chat, and the hands-on actions (laser, gravity switch, moonquake, dust blowing, digging) make each fact something kids can do.

What factors did your team consider?

  1. Audience: simple language and a child-friendly comic style.
  2. Accuracy: facts and coordinates verified through NASA NSSDCA and NASA Science.
  3. Accessibility: works in a browser with no installation.
    Engagement: short chapters with one clear interaction each.
  4. Theme: staying true to "Abandoned but Not Forgotten."
